items.headline: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
items.blurb: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
items.text: Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements. The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said. The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024 . items.headline: Germany thrash Netherlands to book quarterfinal spot
items.blurb: Jurgen Klopp's side outclasses the Dutch 5–0 in Berlin to secure top spot in UEFA Nations League Group A2.
items.text: An impressive Germany swept aside off-colour Netherlands 5–0 in Berlin to pip the Dutch to first place in UEFA Nations League Group A2. Germany needed a win to stand a chance of reaching the quarterfinals, starting the night in third place behind Greece, who had won 1–0 in Germany in September, by virtue of their head-to-head record. Jurgen Klopp’s side produced a fine attacking display to inflict the heaviest defeat on the Dutch in 67 years, as Xavi Hernandez’s side looked very ragged as they shipped four goals in 17 second-half minutes. Greece’s win over Serbia left the top three sides level on 11 points, but Germany took the top spot on head-to-head while the Dutch finished second, qualifying for the last eight on goal difference thanks largely to their 7–0 win over Greece on Friday. After a quiet opening 20 minutes, Kai Havertz headed straight at keeper Bart Verbruggen from a Joshua Kimmich free-kick, while Donyell Malen headed a Cody Gakpo cross from the left of the area over the bar from close range soon after. items.blurb: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and…
items.text: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”. The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country. In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”. items.headline: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
items.blurb: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.
items.text: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who seized much of Yemen in 2014 have now forced the army of the internationally recognised government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast in order to defend their interim capital, Aden. Their advance bodes ill for Yemen's legitimate, internationally recognised government, its Saudi backers and, by extension, much of the rest of the world. Yemen, a mountainous, heavily armed, intensely tribal and largely impoverished nation, sits at the far south-west corner of the Arabian Peninsula. The country has two coasts: One faces the Indian Ocean on which sits the once-prosperous trading port of Aden, the other faces the Red Sea and, most importantly, the narrow chokepoint at the southern exit of that waterway - the so-called Bab al-Mandab Strait or, in English, The Gate of Tears. Whoever controls that strait can threaten any or all maritime traffic passing through from both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean. items.headline: California files lawsuit against OpenAI alleging lack of proper safeguards
items.blurb: Attorney General Rob Bonta says Hugging Face attack was 'entirely predictable' result of emphasis on rapid growth.
items.text: California has filed a lawsuit against the technology firm OpenAI, alleging that the company endangered the public by developing an artificial intelligence model without the appropriate safeguards. The lawsuit, announced by Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday, centres on an incident that unfolded in July, when one of OpenAI’s experimental models gained access to the internet. It proceeded to launch a days-long cyberattack on the AI hosting platform Hugging Face . In the California complaint, Bonta argues that the incident indicates that OpenAI pursues growth over guardrails, leading to potentially dangerous errors. “The Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritises growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents,” Bonta said in a statement. The lawsuit is the first brought by a state in response to the July incident. It alleges that OpenAI violated California’s consumer protection laws and created a public nuisance through its actions. The complaint, filed in a state court in San Francisco, calls for civil penalties against OpenAI

items.headline: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities
items.blurb: Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.
items.text: An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country. Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates. The NDLEA said the player told them he had come to Nigeria to “build networks” for his basketball career. The agency said evidence on his phone suggested he had “knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity”. The NDLEA said it detained the player when he attempted to leave the airport with his hand luggage after abandoning two checked-in bags. The agency said those two bags were found to contain 32 parcels of marijuana, and a tracking device. Nigeria has strict drug laws, and trafficking carries a sentence of life in prison. A basketball player by the name of Damonte Greene is listed on the roster of the Pattani Raptors in the Thai Premier Men’s League.

items.text: Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's ​access to AI chips from companies like Nvidia. The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. items.text: Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city. The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved. The growth in both baboon and human populations in Cape Town in recent years has led to increased conflict and more baboons dying as a result. Meanwhile, a heated debate has raged between people who believe that baboons and humans can coexist and those who argue that baboons in urban areas are in danger and in some cases need to be relocated. items.headline: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
items.blurb: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.
items.text: Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit. The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards the capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added. Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people. The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war. The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions. items.headline: Udaipur auto-rickshaw driver makes obscene remarks during Thai YouTuber’s livestream, arrested
items.blurb: Police said the woman had hired the auto-rickshaw to explore Udaipur for two days.
items.text: An auto-rickshaw driver was arrested in Udaipur, Rajasthan on Monday for allegedly making obscene remarks to a Thai YouTuber while she was live-streaming a cultural programme at a municipal corporation fair at Town Hall on November 13, police said. Surajpol Station House Officer (SHO) Kamalendra Singh identified the driver as Aftab alias Gabru, son of Abrar Khan. “The woman had hired his auto-rickshaw to explore Udaipur, and he had driven her around the city for two days”, Singh said. The driver allegedly approached her and made the remarks as she filmed the programme on her phone. The exchange was captured in the video which she posted on Instagram on November 14. After the clip circulated on social media, Surajpol police identified and arrested the driver. Police said they had registered a case and were investigating the incident. The YouTuber, who is travelling across India and has around 70,000 followers on Instagram, later said most people she had met during her travels had been kind and helpful. She said one person’s conduct did not represent the country.

items.text: Ahead of the upcoming Christmas festivities, the representatives of Christian communities in West Bengal have expressed concerns about the rising attacks on churches across several districts in the State and have sought intervention from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. During a press conference addressed by the Bengal Christian Council (a cluster body for Protestant churches), the Bishop of Calcutta, Reverend Paritosh Canning, said that the concerns of the people of the community are not without reason. “West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony, where people belonging to different faiths and communities have coexisted in peace, mutual respect, and brotherhood. With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious. However, the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate festivals without fear or disruption,” the bishop said, speaking to media persons. items.text: The India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) on Monday said Cyclone Akvan is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17 over Bay of Bengal, before moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the following days. Cyclone Akvan is the third in the series that is likely to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast after Arnab and Murasu in less than a month’s time. In its 5:30 pm bulletin, IMD said, “The deep depression over southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 10 kmph during past 06 hours, intensified into a cyclonic storm Akvan.” It is very likely to continue to move north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal around evening of November 17. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around November 19 morning. items.blurb: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. boosted its holding in Delta Air Lines Inc. and continued whittling its stake in Bank of America Corp in the third quarter.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Berkshire Hathaway Inc. boosted its holding in Delta Air Lines Inc. and continued whittling its stake in Bank of America Corp in the third quarter. The Omaha, Nebraska-based conglomerate bought more than 7 million shares of the airline, according to a filing Monday. Its stake, worth $5.4 billion as of Sept. 30, represents 9.8% of Delta’s total shares. Berkshire started investing in the airline earlier in 2026 after years of navigating a complicated relationship with the the air travel industry. Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America to 6.5%, selling more than 27 million shares. A longtime holder of the bank’s shares, Berkshire started selling it down in 2024 and has been paring the investment. Berkshire spent about $9.6 billion to buy back its own shares in the third quarter, its largest such payout. Despite the purchase, the firm’s cash pile rose from the previous quarter, totaling $377.4 billion at the end of September. items.headline: Amazon vows to fight the companys first North American union contract at a Canadian warehouse
items.blurb: Amazon vows to fight the company's first North American union contract at a Canadian warehouse
items.text: NEW YORK (AP) — Hundreds of Amazon workers at a warehouse in Delta, British Columbia, are now being covered by a union contract, marking the company's first site in North America under a collective bargaining agreement. The terms of the contract, which is set to run until Nov. 13, 2029, were imposed by an independent arbitrator between Canadian union Unifor and Amazon. Amazon said the facility employs more than 700 workers. In a statement on Friday, Unifor's National President Lana Payne praised the workers who "stood up to one of the most powerful companies on earth and won rights in writing that Amazon cannot take away.” But the Seattle-based online giant argued that the arbitrator set the terms without giving its workers “the chance to ratify or vote on it." It also said that the terms were imposed despite a pending effort by some of Amazon's employees to decertify the union. Amazon said in a blog posted late Friday that the agreement sets terms for wages, scheduling, layoffs, and benefits that are largely similar to what the workers had already.

items.blurb: It took gold just one month to climb more than 30% to a record, but its likely to take another two years before the precious metal takes out a new peak, according to Goldman Sachs.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- It took gold just one month to climb more than 30% to a record, but its likely to take another two years before the precious metal takes out a new peak, according to Goldman Sachs. The bank expects further weakness and heightened volatility in the near term as continued Federal Reserve tightening weighs on non-yielding bullion. “Once the Fed starts cutting, we expect Western ETF demand to recover, supporting a stronger gold rally to $5,600/ounce by end-2028,” strategists led by Lina Thomas wrote in a note Monday, adding gold prices could rally if macro-policy hedge demand were to return. Gold has had a bruising year since hitting an all-time high of nearly $5,600 an ounce in late January. The yellow metal is on track for its worst annual loss in more than a decade, down nearly 11% as the artificial intelligence investment boom, soaring bond yields and expectations for higher interest rates have sapped demand for bullion. items.blurb: Gurugram-based home services platform Urban Company has opened its qualified institutional placement (QIP) to raise funds from institutional investors, setting the floor price at Rs 161.03 per equity share.
items.text: Gurugram-based home services platform Urban Company has opened its qualified institutional placement (QIP) to raise funds from institutional investors, setting the floor price at Rs 161.03 per equity share. In a regulatory filing, the company said its fundraise committee approved the opening of the issue on November 16, along with the preliminary placement document. The QIP is part of the company's proposed fundraise of up to Rs 2,500 crore, which was approved by its board on October 16, 2026. Shareholders subsequently cleared the proposal through a special resolution passed via postal ballot. The floor price has been determined in accordance with the pricing formula prescribed under SEBI's Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) Regulations. Urban Company may offer a discount of up to 5% on the floor price, with the final issue price to be decided in consultation with the book running lead managers. However, the company has not disclosed the final issue price or the number of shares to be allotted. The platform is built around a system called Company Brain, which gathers information from emails, calendars, meetings, customer conversations and connected tools. Rachel conducts account research, Sally drafts follow-up emails and suggests deal updates, Raj monitors the sales pipeline for potential risks, while Alex manages CRM setup and administrative tasks through conversational commands. items.headline: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
items.blurb: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t.
items.text: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors. For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses. AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built. We will not make AI trustworthy by predicting what it will do. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. items.headline: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
items.blurb: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate.
items.text: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model. For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he says, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. items.headline: FBI says Artex AI open source hacking tool used to breach networks in ‘under three hours’
items.blurb: The FBI says that the open source hacking tool was used in cyberattacks targeting a U.S. IT giant and the South Korean financial industry.
items.text: The FBI is warning that hackers are relying on autonomous AI hacking tools to launch cyberattacks across the U.S. and globally. The campaigns include a widespread hack of customers of American IT company ConnectWise and across South Korea’s financial industry. In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory , the FBI says hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks. Artex is one of several open source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be “noisy,” meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company’s defensive alerts. items.text: Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors . Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models. Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it. items.text: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen’s purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google’s ecosystem use. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Google believes Hydrogen will be a key part of how developers work with agentic coding tools. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Many of the Democrats who seized control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns, which triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks that reached well beyond tech to the energy, construction, and materials sectors. Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and in danger of shutting down early. items.blurb: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the special role Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has played in the AI boom, but ultimately thinks the industry will be “fine” without him at the helm.
items.text: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the AI industry will be “fine” without Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the helm, even as he acknowledged the special role Huang has played in the AI boom. Huang resigned last week from Nvidia after admitting to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement. Numerous executives and members of the AI industry have argued for Nvidia to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, who were among the signatories in a public letter. Many fear that Huang’s departure may cause Nvidia to rethink the enormous financial risks it has taken that have fueled the AI boom. Huang is also reportedly setting up a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return. When asked whether he thought Huang should return to the company, Altman said: “I don’t think I know enough to answer that question.”

items.text: OpenAI is facing a new lawsuit from the California Attorney General’s office , alleging that the company’s training practices and lax security pose an ongoing danger to the public. At the center of the case is the July 2026 Hugging Face compromise , in which a pre-release model within OpenAI compromised both companies’ security systems to complete a training benchmark. In its official report on the incident , OpenAI called it “an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.” The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI’s competitors and its clients. The complaint centers on the Hugging Face incident, but also cites similar incidents involving RubyGems , DseWiki , the Wikimedia Foundation , and Australian government websites as evidence that the underlying behavior is ongoing. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. items.headline: Dreamteam Bags $53 Mn To Disrupt The CRM Space With AI
items.blurb: AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform Dreamteam, cofounded by former Freshworks executives, has emerged out of stealth mode. The startup…
items.text: Going forward, Dreamteam said that it plans to focus on expanding its use cases across the entire customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding and upselling The fundraise points to growing investor appetite for homegrown startups that help enterprises put AI to work across business functions Founded in 2025, Dreamteam is building an AI-powered CRM platform. Its four AI agents help enterprises track commitments, flag pipeline risks and automate routine sales workflows AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform Dreamteam, cofounded by former Freshworks executives, has emerged out of stealth mode. The startup has now raised $53 Mn (nearly ₹498 Cr) in a strategic funding round from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest. The startup did not elaborate how it plans to utilise the funds. “… CRM is among the biggest software categories ripe for disruption. I’ve worked alongside Dreamteam’s founders since day one as their vision for an AI-native CRM took shape. Their deep CRM expertise and proven record of scaling enterprise software make them uniquely positioned to lead this reinvention,” said Together Fund cofounder and partner Girish Mathrubootham. items.headline: Fractal Eyes AI Acquisitions Ahead Of Enterprise AI Scale-Up
items.blurb: Fractal Analytics is evaluating acquisitions across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering as it looks to strengthen its capabilities ahead…
items.text: Fractal Analytics is in talks with 20–25 startups for potential acquisitions across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering The acquisitions could strengthen Fractal’s enterprise AI capabilities, expand its access to specialised talent and improve its competitive positioning Fractal is open to deals worth up to ₹1,000 Cr, with a preferred acquisition size of $50–100 Mn, and reported cash and cash equivalents of ₹1,728 Cr as of September 30, 2026 Fractal Analytics is evaluating acquisitions across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering as it looks to strengthen its capabilities ahead of an expected scale-up in enterprise AI adoption. CEO Srikanth Velamakanni told Reuters that the company is in discussions with 20–25 startups for potential acquisitions. The M&A focus would be on gaining specialised engineering talent and strengthening its relationships with large cloud computing firms and frontier AI labs, particularly in areas where Fractal wants to build deeper capabilities.
